response.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS a FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark HAVING AVG(remaincount) IS NOT NULL), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m1 FROM per), s1 AS (SELECT per.a AS a, per.a - b1.m1 AS e1 FROM per, b1 WHERE per.a > b1.m1), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m2 FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.a AS a, s1.e1 AS e1, s1.a - b2.m2 AS e2 FROM s1, b2 WHERE s1.a > b2.m2) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_remaining_orders_avg, AVG(e1) AS avg_excess_over_first_benchmark, AVG(e2) AS avg_excess_over_second_benchmark FROM s2

assumptions.assumption: Executions with NULL ordersmark are grouped together as a single pseudo-order (GROUP BY puts NULLs in one group), as the request states.
Orders whose remaincount values are all NULL have no average and are excluded from the benchmark means and from the results.
'Above' means strictly greater than the benchmark mean.
